LANDING PR for story #464, second landing: the journal contention follow-ups #394's bounded settlement left. The ruled bound (three settling patiences, three for a terminal event, three in the lawful end, the 16 MiB hold; the operator's ruling of 2026-09-28) and the seat-record fence are unchanged.

The branch story-464-journal-contention ends at 2098f897, a clean merge of main 77dc2924 (which brings #584), over these commits off main f2b3a387:
- 772c0ac4: story run implement-story-464-journal-cont-cd047fb2 (see the first landing).
- 181f442c: the first landing's fix (landing-pr-for-story-464-the-jou-79c109ca). The quiet-timer test proves the no-wait retry with a peer that lets go of the lock only when told, never by wall clock. That landing ruled residual at LOW, with no security residual and exact coverage, and the operator accepted its three rulings on 2026-10-07 (the store API, the 0029 #464 addendum, the panel parking under 0034 ruling 6).
- a3f94911 (controller): PR #582's baseline-ratchets check failed on the merge with main, because engine/tests.rs came to 6680 lines over main's lowered 6676 baseline. The clean panel member's driver became contention_tests::quiet_command, so engine/tests.rs is back at exactly 6676, with the test's assertions unchanged.
- 37b649f1 and 2098f897: merges of main. Main's clone ratchet was red on a starters/bun.md and python.md pair until #584 re-baselined it.

The only change since the first landing's vouch, other than the merges, is a3f94911, which is test-only and size-neutral.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

The PR's Ruling line will ask the operator for: brokkr-store's public API (+ Chain, Rows, append_chain, append_chain_without_waiting; − append_next_without_waiting); the proposed #464 addendum to decision 0029; and, within it, the behaviour change under decision 0034 ruling 6 that a panel whose member is refused parks, rather than failing retryable, once another member checkpoints after the refusal.

Judge:
1. That the bound and the fence are unchanged: no path holds more than the 16 MiB hold plus one row, no checkpoint lands past a refused row, and the settlement patiences are as ruled.
2. That nothing is lost or reported falsely: every checkpoint either lands, or is counted against its member, who settles indeterminate or fails. An attempt with unjournaled evidence is never a success.
3. That the timer cannot race: the one-second quiet retry uses the no-wait append, the tests use injected time or bounded waits, and no test depends on wall-clock luck under a loaded CI.
4. That the bounded handoff (64) cannot deadlock a driver against its sink or a panel against its members, including at settlement and on a driver that dies.
5. That the chained transaction rolls back whole on any error other than a fence refusal, and commits exactly the rows before a refused one.
6. That the engine.rs hunk is the minimum: decision 0065 slice two's U1g starts on engine.rs soon.
7. That the carried LOWs are listed for the PR, and the addendum says exactly what the code does.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

For the implement phase only: if a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run, all clean:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy on the crates you touched, with -D warnings
- typos --hidden
- quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api

Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

No new regression since the first vouch: the only story change is extracting the checkpoint-free driver into quiet_command; assertions and production journal paths are unchanged. Two carried LOWs remain for the PR. (1) checkpoints.rs:landed and Settled::unjournaled, decision 0071 ruling 8 and 0034 ruling 6: with the journal locked, member Y offers an invalid seat-turn row, then X observes an Unattributable call; release the lock and settle. Y is correctly indeterminate, but its reason falsely says its row came after X's refused checkpoint and omits Y's own fence seq/contract/path. The addendum knowingly keeps the first refusal's site and suppresses the later verdict; carry that reason. Pinned by a_fence_refusal_behind_a_refused_call_is_counted_not_latched_over. (2) checkpoints.rs:drive, task judge 4: an offer callback that panics while a driver sends more than 64 queued checkpoints leaves the receiver alive outside thread::scope; scope waits for the driver blocked in send, hanging instead of propagating the panic. No concrete production callback panic path was found; this is the unchanged carried LOW, not a new security finding. Panel receivers are inside the scope and close on unwind. INFO, carried wording precision: an offer containing a refused call latches without retrying the existing hold; the next offer or quiet timer retries, so addendum rule 1's every-offer wording is broader than this path. Traced the unchanged 16 MiB hold plus one-row allowance, three checkpoint settlement patiences, terminal and lawful-end windows, per-member lost/stranded/dropped accounting, buffered channel drain before settlement, no-wait quiet retry, whole rollback for non-fence errors and prefix commit at a fence refusal. Engine hunk remains 24 added/24 removed at the two sink call sites; no frozen contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json or reference diff. Foreground checks: store chain tests 5 passed, runtime contention/checkpoint/panel-refusal tests 35 passed, cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check passed; git status empty. Full workspace tests and self-bundle compilation rely on supplied VERIFY-PASS; clippy, ratchets, exact coverage and remote CI were not independently rerun here. No high/critical or security residual, no fixes or commits.

Full workspace/self-bundle checks are supplied VERIFY-PASS evidence. Coverage/remote gates not rerun.
No new correctness finding since the first vouch: quiet_command preserves the driver's arguments and outcome, and the panel assertions are unchanged. engine/tests.rs is 6676 lines; engine.rs is 4859 and its feature hunk contains only the two sink integrations. Shared fence/seal follows 0071 ruling 5, Rows.payload is a closure seam (ruling 2), and the API has consumers (ruling 6).
Judges 1-5: 16 MiB and three patiences are unchanged, as are terminal/lawful-end callers. A contended joining row over the hold limit is popped and counted; a lone uncapped row retains #394's exception. Every prospective row is fenced inside the Immediate transaction; refusal commits only the prefix, other errors roll back. Lost/stranded/dropped checkpoints make their owner indeterminate, a refusal fails its owner, and storage failure propagates. take drains until sender disconnection before settlement, retries with the no-wait append, and settlement uses three patient tries. Normal driver death drops the sender; the panel drains despite a refusal/failure. The revised quiet test injects zero interval and orders peer release on append three, asserting exact calls and told-not-outlasted; the recorded compiling patient-retry mutation fails at 2 versus 3. No mutations performed here.
Surviving findings, all carried for the PR:
(1) LOW, checkpoints.rs landed/unjournaled, 0071 ruling 8 and 0034 ruling 6: a held Y row predating X's refused call, later fence-refused itself, is reported as coming after X's refusal; Y's own seq/schema/path verdict is lost. Fail closed: Y is indeterminate and the row never lands. Implementer reason: addendum rule 3 deliberately preserves the first refusal/site, pinned by a_fence_refusal_behind_a_refused_call_is_counted_not_latched_over.
(2) LOW, checkpoints.rs drive, task judge 4 and 0071 ruling 9: receiver outside thread::scope survives a sink-offer panic while scope joins a driver blocked on a full handoff. Panel receiver is inside its scope and drops on unwind. No concrete production sink panic path found; normal driver death is safe. This remains the exceptional-path residual from the first landing.
(3) INFO, addendum rule 1: an offer carrying a refused call latches and returns without retrying the preceding hold; next offer or quiet tick retries. 'Each time any site hands over another checkpoint' is broader than code for that offer.
(4) INFO, hold: a lone held row is serialized again after each joining row is popped for exceeding the limit. Cost only; bound cannot drift.
(5) INFO: the 64-row handoff is a count bound, not a byte bound; uncapped rows sit beside the hold. Addendum rules 4/5 disclose this. The exact one-second constant has no separate test pin; the injected interval proves the retry path.
Unchanged #394 limitations to carry: settlement impossible while nothing is writable beyond the windows; spill/attempt-wide bounds belong to #433; writer-order ticket considered and not built; USER identity residual belongs to 0025. The addendum is proposed, names the API and panel-park consequence under 0034 ruling 6; supplied operator acceptance of the first landing's three rulings is respected. members.glm:
Correctness review of 77dc2924..2098f897 (the #464 second landing: branch commits + a3f94911 + the two merges). Read-only: no tracked file changed, no commit; git status clean after every check. What I did: read the full 12-file diff, the current chain.rs/checkpoints.rs/engine.rs and both test suites, the 0029 addendum rule-by-rule against the code, the first landing's ledger (.forge/ledger/landing-pr-for-story-464-the-jou-79c109ca.md) for the carried findings, and the merges' conflict resolutions; re-ran in the foreground: cargo test -p brokkr-store --lib -- chain:: (5 passed), cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib -- engine::contention_tests engine::checkpoints a_panel_members_refused_checkpoint_fails_that_member_alone (35 passed), and quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api on the pinned nightly (all hold — the clones ratchet that a3f94911's message left red is green now that #584 is merged).

Seven points judged. (1) Bound and fence unchanged: HELD_BYTES 16 MiB and SETTLING_PATIENCES 3 untouched; hold() keeps held_bytes <= limit or exactly one unmeasured row, popping and counting lost only the newcomer, so no path holds more than the 16 MiB hold plus one row; chain::fence is the old fence verbatim, judging every row at head+1 inside the same Immediate transaction, and chain_once breaks at the refusal before sealing, so nothing lands past a refused row; terminal-event and lawful-end patiences in engine.rs are outside the diff. (2) Nothing lost or falsely reported: every checkpoint lands, is held and retried, or is counted lost/stranded/dropped by site, and any count turns that site's outcome indeterminate (never its driver's success); the refused site fails on its refusal; a storage failure fails the attempt from settle(); an unjournaled attempt is never a success.
